classification.difficultyReason: Factor non-monic quadratics, average their zeroes and substitute to determine exact vertices before sketching.

content.prompt: Use factoring to sketch the graphs of the following non-monic quadratic functions, clearly indicating the vertex and the intercepts with the axes.

answer.worked:
The coefficient of $x^2$ is positive, so the curve is concave up.
$$\begin{align*}y&=(2x+5)(x+1)\\0&=(2x+5)(x+1)\\x&=-\frac52\text{ or }-1\end{align*}$$
At $x=0$, $y=5$. The axis is midway between the zeroes:
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{-\frac52-1}{2}\\x&=-\frac74\\y&=\left(2\left(-\frac74\right)+5\right)\left(-\frac74+1\right)\\y&=-\frac98\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(-\frac74,-\frac98)$.

spec.description: Complete solution sketch with both zeroes, y-intercept and vertex; no grid.

$$\begin{align*}y&=(2x-1)(x+3)\\0&=(2x-1)(x+3)\\x&=\frac12\text{ or }-3\end{align*}$$
At $x=0$, $y=-3$. The axis is midway between the zeroes:
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{\frac12-3}{2}\\x&=-\frac54\\y&=\left(2\left(-\frac54\right)-1\right)\left(-\frac54+3\right)\\y&=-\frac{49}{8}\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(-\frac54,-\frac{49}{8})$.

At $x=0$, $y=-8$. The axis is midway between the zeroes:

answer.worked:
The coefficient of $x^2$ is positive, so the curve is concave up.
$$\begin{align*}y&=2(x-3)(x+3)\\0&=2(x-3)(x+3)\\x&=3\text{ or }-3\\x&=\frac{3-3}{2}\\x&=0\end{align*}$$
At $x=0$, $y=-18$. The axis is $x=0$, so the vertex and $y$-intercept are both $(0,-18)$.

answer.worked:
The coefficient of $x^2$ is positive, so the curve is concave up.
$$\begin{align*}y&=(3x+4)(x-1)\\0&=(3x+4)(x-1)\\x&=-\frac43\text{ or }1\end{align*}$$
At $x=0$, $y=-4$. The axis is midway between the zeroes:
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{-\frac43+1}{2}\\x&=-\frac16\\y&=\left(3\left(-\frac16\right)+4\right)\left(-\frac16-1\right)\\y&=-\frac{49}{12}\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(-\frac16,-\frac{49}{12})$.

answer.worked:
The coefficient of $x^2$ is negative, so the curve is concave down.
$$\begin{align*}y&=-(4x^2-7x+3)\\y&=-(4x-3)(x-1)\\0&=-(4x-3)(x-1)\\x&=\frac34\text{ or }1\end{align*}$$
At $x=0$, $y=-3$. The axis is midway between the zeroes:
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{\frac34+1}{2}\\x&=\frac78\\y&=-\left(4\left(\frac78\right)-3\right)\left(\frac78-1\right)\\y&=\frac1{16}\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(\frac78,\frac1{16})$.
